title: Year alignment reduced late-season deficit variance by 41% at three Arctic gauges in 1980-2011, with mixed test support
abstract: We tested whether seasonal low-flow deficit volumes align across Ob-Salekhard, Lena-Kyusyur and Yenisey-Igarka. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 and 31 common complete certified years in 1980-2011. August-October deficit volume was flow missing below a held-out-year calendar-day 20th percentile. After time-group means were removed, the variance of the summed deficit was 0.591 times the sum of separate variances. Independent matching of river-years has an exact expected ratio of one. The observed excess was -40.9%, with a two-sided conditional permutation p-value of 0.0558. Two of six planned checks had unadjusted p-values below 0.05; the other four did not. The result suggests offsetting shortages, with mixed test support. This extends published tests of low-flow day counts and spell lengths to missing water volume on the same data. It does not establish independence, a cause, a trend or ocean response. Short records, fitted thresholds, regulation, flow error and conditional exchangeability limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure and an independent CSV audit support reproduction. External records and river-year derivatives stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Observed excess variance of summed deficit volume and the conditional independent year-pairing reference. Blue intervals are null ranges, not effect confidence intervals.
